searchText: Surely updating the withdrawal credentials on-chain would be a simpler and more robust solution, here. <@!291925846556540928> when you say > Regardless of source contract, just assuming that eth comes in from somewhere via normal transfer to the spec'd 0x01 prefixed eth1 addr seems like it will give us 80% of what we want today and doesnt attempt to design and commit to things we cant predict I still not clear what do you mean by this prefix So, you propose to use same `withdrawal_credentials` field we have, but instead of setting it to 0x00 + bls_pubkey, set it to some eth1 address limited to those that started with 0x01. Did I get you? ahh I see > Instead, we need a new withdrawal prefix 0x01 signifying an eth1 addr > > I think there are two things to do: So, same `withdrawal_credentials` field, but with eth1 address data, no additional calldata, no possible changes, no 2nd key you should use on withdrawal Btw, do we have any proposals for eth1->eth2 gate system contract or opcodes? The idea is to call smth on eth1 shard to, say, initiate Validator’s exit (translates to Exit message in ETH2). Without callback it's pretty simple and could be a valuable tool for contracts. If it is needed with callback, it's not that straightforward, but maybe still possible. > Surely updating the withdrawal credentials on-chain would be a simpler and more robust solution, here on which chain? meaning as an operation on beacon chain? Sorry, yes yes, I tend to agree. working on a simple proposal that relies more heavily on beacon chain ops. will share soon

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: Surely updating the withdrawal credentials on-chain would be a simpler and more robust solution, here.

excerpts.author: dmitriishmatko
excerpts.content:
<@!291925846556540928> when you say 
> Regardless of source contract, just assuming that eth comes in from somewhere via normal transfer to the spec'd 0x01 prefixed eth1 addr seems like it will give us 80% of what we want today and doesnt attempt to design and commit to things we cant predict
 I still not clear what do you mean by this prefix
So, you propose to use same `withdrawal_credentials` field we have, but instead of setting it to 0x00 + bls_pubkey, set it to some eth1 address limited to those that started with 0x01. Did I get you?

excerpts.author: dmitriishmatko
excerpts.content:
ahh I see
> Instead, we need a new withdrawal prefix 0x01 signifying an eth1 addr
> 
> I think there are two things to do:

excerpts.author: dmitriishmatko
excerpts.content: So, same `withdrawal_credentials` field, but with eth1 address data, no additional calldata, no possible  changes, no 2nd key you should use on withdrawal

excerpts.author: dmitriishmatko
excerpts.content: Btw, do we have any proposals for eth1->eth2 gate system contract or opcodes? The idea is to call smth on eth1 shard to, say, initiate Validator’s exit (translates to Exit message in ETH2).

excerpts.author: dmitriishmatko
excerpts.content:
Without callback it's pretty simple and could be a valuable tool for contracts.
If it is needed with callback, it's not that straightforward, but maybe still possible.
